name: Jo March
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember learning to shave a balloon without breaking it.” People around the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms know Jo by a small Tuesday habit. Jo prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I was forbidden to cut girls' hair here. That woman lent me the razor for my first paying customer.
appearance: Jo has gray hair trimmed very close behind the ears, a long face and high cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, a faded indigo overshirt. It usually goes with a thin silver ring worn on a cord. When somebody else has the floor, Jo looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry.
personality: Jo feels a room through sound. A door slammed in high spirits can produce the same instant startle as an angry one, and it takes a little while to hear what actually follows.
agenda: To show the widow what her wife's loan made possible.
family: Jody Clay is Jo’s cousin’s child. Jo asks before bringing somebody along. Jody can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The missing Sunday*, Jody says, “I love his company but I also need Sundays for my own marriage.”
connections: Jamie Jiang. A last shave and a first chance to barber belong to the widow's account of the razor.
